thread:
Theo: Dropping a new mock for the usage & billing header — thinking about a single responsive control area that contains: scope (Org / Project pill), date range, unit toggle (Tokens / USD), and a compact download menu. Goal: reduce visual clutter but keep export discoverable. Figma: https://www.figma.com/file/usage-header-new (page 'Unified Header').

Jin: Nice compact direction. Two immediate thoughts: 1) Screen real estate: on desktops the header can be two rows (filters row + actions row) to avoid cramming. 2) Download discoverability: a lone caret is easy to miss; we should keep a visible label like "Download" with a caret and a small badge indicating default format (CSV).

Harper: Copy nit: if we show unit toggle, label should be explicit "Show as: Tokens | USD" rather than just icons. Many users misinterpret the iconography. Also propose adding contextual hint under the header: "Data reflects model pricing as of selected date" — reduces confusion when costs change after model pricing updates.

Marta: Perf/backend: when users switch units we currently re-request metrics and recompute costs on the server. That can be slow. Suggest sending both token and cost metrics in the same payload and let the client toggle formats without refetch. It increases payload size but reduces perceived latency. We can gzip and paginate.

Theo: Good point. Let's plan to return both metrics. Jin — can you mock the header with a two-row variant and a mobile collapsed variant? Put the Download label on the action row with a small CSV chip by default.

Jin: Will do. Also accessibility: when the download menu opens it must announce the selected scope and date-range (e.g., "Download invoice for Org: X, Date: Apr 1Apr 30"). a11y-bot, can you add that to checks?

a11y-bot: queued accessibility scan for branch feature/unified-usage-header. Preliminary: download button needs aria-haspopup and aria-expanded updating. Unit toggle should be a role="segmentedcontrol" with keyboard left/right behavior. Header lacks a skip-link region for screen-reader users to jump to the chart. Full report: https://ci.redwood.ai/a11y/699.

Harper: Regarding invoices: let's change button copy from "Download invoice" to "Download (CSV)" with caret menu that expands to "Download (CSV)", "Download (PDF)", and "Download per-project CSV". Default action should start CSV stream and show a non-blocking toast with a link. Copy for toast: "Invoice CSV is generating — download available here." Include keyboard focus on toast when it appears.

Marta: Backend: PDF generation is queued; we must surface expected wait time in the menu (e.g., "PDF (may take up to 2 minutes)"). Per-project CSV will be a streaming endpoint; we'll provide a signed URL in response. Also will add request_id in response headers for telemetry.

Theo: UX edge-case: when the user is scoped to multiple projects (multi-select), what does CSV mean? Proposal: default to rollup and expose a menu item "Download separate CSVs per project" which triggers a zipping job. Make the menu item descriptive: "Per-project CSV (zipped)". Jin, show that in the mock.

Jin: Added the two-row desktop layout, mobile collapsed header, and the menu states in Figma. Also added high-contrast variants and focus styles. Uploading updated frames now.

a11y-bot: re-run queued. New scan: segmented control keyboard behavior OK, download menu has aria labels, but color contrast for the CSV chip still fails at 12px on some themes. Recommend using 14px or bumping weight.

Marta: I'll coordinate with infra to ensure the combined payload shape includes token_count, cost_usd, and pricing_version. infra-bot, can you pre-warm the streaming endpoint for large orgs?

infra-bot: pre-warm job queued for /exports/stream and /exports/zip on staging. Preview build: https://staging.redwood.ai/preview/699 (build #699).

Theo: Thanks team. Action items: Jin (two-row + mobile mocks + menu microcopy), Marta (payload + endpoints + ETA in menu), Harper (copy tweaks + toast text), a11y-bot (final scan and keyboard walkthrough). We'll review in tomorrow's design crit. :tada:
